newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope looks fit at first appearance since flu.
newsitem.headline: Pope looks fit at first appearance since flu.

text.p: Pope John Paul looked fit on Sunday at his first appearance since being laid low by influenza last week.

The Pope, 76, spoke forcefully during his Sunday angelus from the window of his apartments overlooking the Vatican's St Peter's Square and further indicated he was ready to return to his full schedule by referring to future appointments.
The leader of the world's 960 million Roman Catholics cancelled his general audience on Wednesday because of influenza and a sore throat. Doctors ordered him to stay in bed for a few days.
The Pontiff, without referring to his health problems, on Sunday urged followers to show more compassion to the sick, terminally ill and disabled.

"We know through experience that in sickness one needs not only adequate treatment but also human warmth," he said. "In current society, there is the often the risk of loosing true contact with others. The pace of work, stress, family crises make it even more difficult to be together in a brotherly fashion."
The Pope said he chose his topic for the angelus to mark "World Day for the Sick" later this month.

At the end, the Pope made off-the-cuff remarks in his native Polish, reminding pilgrims in the square that he would be coming home to Poland this spring. Reverting back to Italian, he also said he would begin the season of Lent in Ash Wednesday services this week.
The Pontiff is scheduled to visit Poland May 31-June 10, one of several overseas trips he has planned this year.
The Vatican has also confirmed trips to Sarajevo, Prague, Paris and Brazil and the Pope is expected to make a brief visit to Lebanon this spring.
Doctors who removed the Pope's appendix last October had urged the Pontiff, the most travelled in history, to slow down.
